Task description: Use the right arm to pick up the black-and-gray mouse at the lower right of the view, place it on the blue rectangular mat at the upper left, and adjust its orientation.

Success criteria: The mouse lands near the center of the blue mat, flat with its long axis aligned to the mat's long edge. It has been released, and both grippers are open.

## Execution tips

- Approach from above if possible and grip the flatter sides around the middle of the mouse shell across its width. Set the opening slightly wider than the grasp area, avoiding a grasp only on the curved top, buttons, or scroll wheel.
- Before closing, confirm that the fingers are on opposite sides of the mouse and the pads can contact its sides, leaving clearance between the fingertips and table to avoid pressing it down or pushing it away.
- Adjust the orientation where the mouse is off the table and there is room to turn, reducing scraping and slipping caused by rotating it against the tabletop.
- The blue mat is narrow. When placing, check the mouse’s position relative to the mat center from above, and release only after it is supported near the surface to reduce shifting or turning after a drop.
